_what: The live catalog state, read from the provisioned Postgres. The text lint reads migration files; this is what the database actually became. A rule asserted against text and a rule asserted against the catalog are different rules, and only the second one is true.
_staleness: taken_against_migrations must equal the digest of db/foundation/migrations/*.sql. If a migration changes and this file is not retaken, db-schema-lint FAILS. A snapshot that can silently describe a database that no longer exists is the same defect class as a blocker list nobody re-checks.
_measurement_note:
service_roles.has_password is read from pg_authid, NOT pg_roles. pg_roles is a view that replaces rolpassword with the literal '********', so the obvious query reports a password on every role including ones that have none. The first attempt here made exactly that mistake and reported has_password: true for all three.

Retaken 2026-09-06 after batch 004. Batch 004 asserts and changes nothing, so the catalog below is expected to be identical -- and it was RE-READ rather than carried forward, because a snapshot copied across a migration is exactly the thing the staleness digest exists to catch. Two fields are new and one was wrong: service_roles now carry `superuser` (measured false for all three), the instance's `roles_superuser` set is recorded (supabase_admin alone), and the old `memberships: 0` is replaced by `grants_to_admin`, which is 2 for each role -- the CREATE ROLE grant and the explicit re-grant from batch 003. A1's countersignature noted the zero contradicted six live pg_auth_members rows; it counted the wrong direction and no rule read it.

Extended 2026-09-06 for RFC-2026-019 §5. Three fields, all read from the instance: each tenant table's owner, the roles authenticator is a member of, and the owner already recorded on every SECURITY DEFINER function. The second is the decision itself as a measurement -- authenticator is a member of anon, authenticated and service_role and of NO service role -- and the rule that reads it is the only form in which 'we did not grant it' can fail a build.

not_applied_to_this_instance.why:
BATCH 020 IS DECLARED HERE FOR A REASON THAT FOLLOWS FROM 011's RATHER THAN REPEATING IT. 020 depends on 011: every one of its ten policies resolves membership through app.is_active_member or app.workspace_member_role, which are functions owned by app_authz, which does not exist on this instance. Applying 020 here would either fail outright or -- worse -- require applying 011 first, which is the thing the paragraph below says is not done. A batch cannot be applied to a database that is missing the batch it is built on, so the declaration extends to the tail rather than making an exception for it.

WHAT THIS COSTS FOR 020 SPECIFICALLY, stated rather than absorbed: the four tables batch 020 creates are NOT in `tenant_tables` below, because they are not on this instance and this file records measurements and not intentions. There is no `business_profiles` row here for the same reason there is no `authz` block. The rules that would read those rows -- RLS enabled and forced, a primary key, an owner comment, a recorded owner -- are asked WHERE THEY CAN BE, and the honest inventory is three places rather than one. `schemaLint` holds the owner comment, ENABLE, FORCE and the primary key from the migration TEXT on every `npm run check`. 020's own apply-time `do $$` block asserts ENABLE, FORCE, the absent version-table grants and RFC-2026-017 §3's owner rule against the LIVE catalog of whatever database receives it, which on every pull request is the postgres:17 service container `make db-migrate-clean` builds. There is no live tenant-table measurement of that container and this file does not claim one: unlike batch 011, whose §6.1 rules had no text form at all and therefore needed `scripts/db/authz-proofs.mjs`, every per-table rule here already has both a text form and an apply-time form. `scripts/db/run.mjs` checks the two directions that make the absence honest: every table created by a migration this instance HAS received must appear below, and a table appearing below that no such migration creates is a finding. So `tenant_tables` cannot silently fail to grow -- the moment 020 reaches this instance and the snapshot is retaken, its four tables are required here.

Batch 011 is the first migration in this repository that is deliberately NOT applied to the provisioned instance. CI is its proof surface: RFC-2026-020's approval is conditional on §6.2, which must be discharged by EXECUTION, and one of the two proofs constructs a recursive policy on app.workspace_members in order to observe 42P17. Constructing a known-broken authorization policy on a live database to prove it is broken is not something a batch does to prove itself, and applying an unmerged authorization boundary to a live database so that a lint passes is the inversion the lint exists to prevent. The batch is applied to the postgres:17 service container on every pull request, where db-migrate-clean applies it and scripts/db/authz-proofs.mjs measures the result.

WHAT THIS COSTS, stated rather than absorbed: taken_against_migrations is the digest of the migration set WITHOUT the batches named here, so this snapshot no longer describes the whole of db/foundation/migrations. Nothing is weakened -- a batch the instance HAS received must still be in the digest, an undeclared change to one still fails exactly as before, and the declaration itself is checked: it must name files that exist and must name a TAIL of the ordered set, because a database missing a middle batch while holding later ones is DIVERGENT rather than behind, which is a different finding with a different fix.

WHAT IS NOT HERE, and why that is the point: there is no `authz` block below. app_authz does not exist on this instance and schema app holds no function there (both measured 2026-09-06, read-only). RFC-2026-020 §6.1/1-6 are properties of a database that HAS batch 011, so they are asked of the CI container, which can answer them, rather than answered here with fields nobody measured. scripts/db/run.mjs refuses an authz block while this declaration stands, and REQUIRES one the moment it is removed.

platform_auth_uid.definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auth.uid()
 RETURNS uuid
 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE
AS $function$
  select 
  coalesce(
    nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub', true), ''),
    (nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'sub')
  )::uuid
$function$

_role_scoped_policies_note:
One entry per (policy, table, role) pair in schema app, read from pg_policy 2026-09-06. Two rules read it. The exemption register's corroboration rule reads it as the OTHER evidence a row naming a role can be checked against -- RFC-2026-016 §4 calls a policy on a named role the sanctioned form of a bypass, and until batch 011 the rule recognised only the role ATTRIBUTE, which is the form §4 was replacing. And the completeness pass reads it in the second direction: a policy naming a role outside the request path owes the register a row.

Every one of the ten names `authenticated`, so the completeness pass passes VACUOUSLY today. That is recorded rather than glossed: it is the measured state of this instance, and it stops being vacuous the moment batch 011 reaches it and app_authz's single policy appears here, which is exactly when the register owes that row.
_platform_auth_uid_note: RFC-2026-020 §5/4 inlines this function's request.jwt.claims branch into batch 011, because no role our migrations create can call auth.uid(): schema auth is owned by supabase_admin and postgres holds USAGE on it WITHOUT grant option, so no migration of ours can grant it (measured 2026-09-06). The cost of a copy is that the original can move and nothing would notice. This field is what turns that cost into a build failure -- run.mjs compares the recorded body against the constant batch 011 copied a branch of. It is read verbatim from pg_get_functiondef and is NOT the CI shim's version, which differs: the shim reads only request.jwt.claims and uses ::json rather than ::jsonb, so comparing against the container would pin the wrong function.
_membership_note:
members_besides_admin counts roles granted membership in the service role OTHER than the administrative role, and it is 0: nothing can become app_worker except postgres, which is how the isolation suite assumes it. grants_to_admin is 2 for each -- the CREATE ROLE admin grant (set false, inherit false) and batch 003's explicit re-grant (set true, inherit false), measured 2026-09-06.

The field these replace was `memberships: 0`, which counted the OTHER direction -- roles the service role is itself a member of. That is trivially zero, was read by no rule, and A1's countersignature noted it contradicted six live pg_auth_members rows. A number nobody reads is not evidence, and a number that reads the wrong direction while looking right is worse.
